sections.Profile:
Humpty Dumpty , released by D. Gottlieb & Co. in October 1947, is a one-player electro-mechanical game and the first pinball machine with electrically powered, player-controlled flippers, an innovation credited to Harry Mabs: six of them, three on each side facing outward, worked by buttons on the cabinet. Roy Parker drew the artwork, and Gottlieb built 6,500.
